CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in both hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
60-year-old right-handed male with several weeks of numbness and tingling in both hands, worse since a car accident last December when he broke both wrists. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring fingers. Patient reports soreness, occasional throbbing, and weakness, especially with use. Tingling is more pronounced when painful and becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms occur primarily at night and come and go throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity. Also reports mild stiffness in neck since hitting his head during the accident (noted as contusion at that time). Currently wearing splints on both wrists, right worse than left, which provide some relief. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medication but has not been taking it as directed. Symptoms have worsened significantly over the last month.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. GI: excessive appetite and bloating. Endocrine: always hungry. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems is negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral wrist fractures from motor vehicle accident in December (previous year). Head contusion from same accident. Prediabetes (controlled with diet changes). Hypertension. Anxiety.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medication (prescribed but not taken as directed).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic: Sensation normal except pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on the right and decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on the left. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities, 2+ in knees, toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of exam normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to past wrist trauma. Plan includes: (1) Schedule EMG test to determine exact location of nerve irritation and pinpoint nerve issues; (2) Return for follow-up visit after testing; (3) If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options; (4) Continue wearing splints on both wrists.
